covers: Front-of-shirt sponsor; Etihad Stadium and Etihad Campus naming rights
signed: Original agreement announced July 2011 (expanding an earlier shirt-sponsorship arrangement)
reported_value_html: Reported as £400m over 10 years for the combined package (shirt, stadium naming and the Etihad Campus training complex), per Campaign; a separate report put the stadium-naming-rights portion alone at £150m over 10 years, per Al Jazeera — sources differ on how the total splits across components. Details of a renegotiated deal for the following decade, reported at roughly £350m, emerged in City's 2020 CAS appeal papers rather than any public announcement, per Forbes. Following a September 2025 settlement between City and the Premier League over Associated Party Transaction (APT) rules, a further renewal was reported as "close to £1bn" — a figure not officially disclosed by either party, per SportsPro.
allegation_html: The Der Spiegel/Football Leaks documents (published November 2018) alleged that Manchester City's ownership group, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), covertly funded the large majority of Etihad's reported annual sponsorship fee rather than Etihad itself — reported as roughly £8m paid directly by Etihad against a total annual fee of around £67.5m, with the remainder said to come from ADUG — effectively disguising ownership investment as sponsorship income for Financial Fair Play purposes, according to SportBusiness's coverage of the leak.

covers: Early-era commercial partner (UAE state-linked telecommunications company)
signed: Sponsorship dating from the club's early Abu Dhabi-ownership seasons; no single announcement date confirmed
reported_value_html: No standalone reported value specific to Etisalat has been confirmed. Coverage of the Football Leaks documents referenced a combined figure of around £120m in sponsorship income across four Abu Dhabi-linked partners (Etisalat, Etihad, Aabar Investments and the Abu Dhabi Tourism Authority) for the 2012–13 financial years, without breaking out Etisalat's individual share.
allegation_html: The same November 2018 Der Spiegel/Football Leaks reporting alleged that Etisalat's sponsorship income, like Etihad's, was inflated or routed through the ownership group to disguise direct investment as commercial revenue for Financial Fair Play purposes — see Sports Illustrated's coverage of the leaked documents.

covers: Commercial partner; became a focus of the 2023–25 Associated Party Transactions (APT) dispute
signed: Proposed sponsorship submitted to the Premier League for approval in 2023
reported_value_html: No specific reported deal value for this sponsorship has been confirmed. Its significance here is regulatory rather than financial: the Premier League rejected the proposed deal in 2023 on fair-market-value grounds, and an independent tribunal ruled on 7 October 2024 that the rejection had been reached in a procedurally unfair manner (without ruling on the deal's value itself) — a decision reported by the Malay Mail and legal analysts including HCR Law.
